# The reading room

Research for Atul Kanodia, 21 September 2026.

All 30 supplied links were recovered: 27 X roots, with linked author continuations, quoted articles and a public sample of replies, plus three Instagram posts. Instagram required a browser route after anonymous extraction failed; the browser itself remained logged out. This is an original, organized digest, not a full republication of third-party threads. Spanish material is summarized in English. Numerical earnings claims are attributed to their authors, not verified results.

The public reply sample is incomplete. A missing answer means it was not exposed in the retrieved sample, not that no answer exists anywhere. Image text was OCR-read; OCR can lose punctuation and small labels. Seventeen distinct linked videos were downloaded: fifteen from X roots and related posts, plus the two Instagram reels. Representative frames were inspected and speech-bearing streams were transcribed locally. Automated transcripts are fallible; visual checks corrected the Picsart product name. Full copyrighted transcripts are not republished.

## What I would keep

For YouTube, the most useful combination is a repeatable question, a specific audience and a story with changing stakes. The product-science format fits your hardware and markets interests particularly well. Make one pilot you can inspect before increasing output. Treat the revenue screenshots and universal RPM claims as marketing until attributable analytics establish otherwise.

Website direction updated 22 September: a relaxed personal page about coding and AI experiments. The meowls are animated characters in short interactive scenes. A fictional interview introduces HALO; a pathfinder introduces Botato; the hardware hunt combines liquidation and GPU flipping. These scenes illustrate the projects without connecting to live tools.

For AI workflows, preserve sources, define the responsibility and evaluate the output. The strongest ideas here are ordinary engineering discipline expressed through new interfaces. Repeated self-scoring is not an external quality test.

## A small YouTube experiment

1. Pick one real question with visible trade-offs: why a seemingly cheap GPU can cost more to run, how auction fees change a bid, or why a keyboard switch feels different.
2. Gather sources and record the exact claims the script must support. Label fictional stories clearly when using the Last Shift format.
3. Write the first conflict and the promised resolution. Outline the decisions between them before choosing a runtime.
4. Produce a short representative sequence with consistent characters, understandable narration and editable visuals. Compare the export with the source claims.
5. Publish through your normal channel workflow when ready. Use audience response and the retention curve to choose the next change. No channel was created or video uploaded during this task.

### What makes those AI short stories?

[Original source: @fedeogue](https://x.com/fedeogue/status/2098870098442240124)

The useful answer is in the Spanish replies: generation, narration and editing are separate jobs.

Federico asks which tool produces the illustrated story format shown in the screenshot. The examples package topics such as startup founders, insurance actuaries and family offices as explanatory stories. The root is a question, not a tutorial or a verified attribution of the example videos.

**Replies and continuation.** Replies suggest Google Flow; another proposes Veo 3 for shots, ElevenLabs for narration and CapCut for editing and subtitles. A third names KorpiAI. These are recommendations from commenters, not evidence that the displayed channels use them.

**Assessment.** Useful tool leads. Compare one short scene for character consistency, editability and cost before committing to a complete production pipeline.

### POV explainers: a format, not a niche

[Original source: @Kingofytauto](https://x.com/Kingofytauto/status/2098725158462632188)

Second-person explanations can turn money, work or social systems into a concrete situation.

The image shows packaged wealth and lifestyle explanations, including old money and retiring early. The transferable pattern is to put the viewer inside a role or predicament and explain the decisions that follow. The post itself contains almost no production method.

**Replies and continuation.** Visible replies ask about approximate revenue per thousand views and whether the author owns the channel. No substantive answer was exposed.

**Assessment.** Good packaging reference. Channel ownership, earnings, retention and repeatability remain unverified.

### The claimed $41k faceless-channel workflow

[Original source: @naiem_bn](https://x.com/naiem_bn/status/2098953965077774693)

A five-part thread covers niches, scripts, voice, visuals, editing and batching.

The author recommends finance, technology and business; a roughly 1,500-word script with an immediate conflict; continuing curiosity; conversational narration; generated stills; selective animation; and editing in CapCut or Premiere. The named stack includes Claude, ElevenLabs, Midjourney or Flux, and Runway or Pika. Later replies emphasize batching and spending substantial effort on titles and thumbnails.

**Replies and continuation.** The main author continuation was recovered. Its final point leaves curation, positioning and editorial judgment with the creator. The visible outside reply adds encouragement rather than evidence.

**Assessment.** Treat the $41,000/month headline and proposed RPM ranges as unaudited marketing claims. The thread supplies no attributable channel financials. Its blanket suggestion that a model avoids hallucinations is not a valid quality guarantee. The usable part is the production sequence, with independent fact checking.

### Simple 2D animation, long-form questions

[Original source: @CalliopeLabsyt](https://x.com/CalliopeLabsyt/status/2098917072591823262)

One strong question can organize a longer illustrated explanation.

Calliope promotes an idea-to-script-to-visuals-to-animation workflow. The quoted example is a Neon Rush video about how humans reached the Americas, with a screenshot showing about 135K views and 22.2K subscribers. The post argues that simple motion can support a 20-minute-plus story; complexity of animation is not its core selling point.

**Replies and continuation.** Commenters ask about production cost and audience retention. The exposed replies do not resolve either. A screenshot of views does not establish profitability or retention. The 34-second demo shows an editing timeline and narrated prehistoric migration claims; those scientific claims were not independently checked.

**Assessment.** Useful long-form reference and a vendor demo. Evaluate a sample sequence for factual sourcing, visual continuity and editable output before paying for scale.

### Wild West stories and repeatable packaging

[Original source: @MuteeAutomation](https://x.com/MuteeAutomation/status/2098829809551802419)

Find an overlooked story, make its stakes clear, then compare results across uploads.

The screenshot names Doodle Gulch and shows 17 videos, roughly 449 subscribers and one video around 141K views. The described process researches existing viewer clicks, looks for topic gaps, uses curiosity-led titles and recognizable illustrated thumbnails, and iterates from results.

**Replies and continuation.** The visible replies mostly request the advertised kit. They add no useful detail about costs, retention or the channel’s other videos.

**Assessment.** Useful example of a narrow editorial promise. One winning upload is not a reliable forecast for a new channel, and the post is also a lead-generation funnel.


### Story hooks, angles and title formulas

[Original source: @thegoldeenhand](https://x.com/thegoldeenhand/status/2098871078835957924)

Choose the angle and stakes before stretching a topic into a long script.

The author claims testing more than 300 videos. Suggested hooks establish a time and place, a disadvantaged protagonist, an internal flaw or a deadline. Formats include a single event, biography, mystery and comparison. Suggested lengths span roughly 20–60 minutes. The post also lists romance, military, crime, empire, survival and horror niches with claimed RPM bands.

**Replies and continuation.** Visible replies are appreciative rather than analytical. There is no underlying test set, revenue distribution or comparison controlling for channel size.

**Assessment.** Keep the hook taxonomy and the instruction to assess click-through and watch behavior. Do not use the listed RPM bands as a budget or assume that a long duration creates value. The paid-community promotion is part of the context.


### Make the audience more specific

[Original source: @boomerrbryan](https://x.com/boomerrbryan/status/2099140543725109544)

An over-55 audience changes the questions a video should answer.

The post proposes age-specific versions of investing, technology, cooking and physical-activity content, then monetization beyond ads through services, leads and affiliates. The useful editorial idea is to address a real situation rather than merely append an age bracket to a title.

**Replies and continuation.** The author follows with a Subscribr referral. A commenter challenges the incentive to publicize a supposedly easy, underexploited opportunity.

**Assessment.** The claims of almost no competition, unusually high ad value and easy profits are unsupported in the post. Audience needs require research; age is not a substitute for a specific problem.

[Original source: @itsolelehmann](https://x.com/itsolelehmann/status/2099117750824165457)

The idea is to give an editing agent footage and concrete timeline instructions.

The root describes installing Resolve and an MCP integration, providing a footage folder, finding appropriate B-roll, and asking for edits. Its casual setup instructions omit implementation details and compatibility requirements.

**Replies and continuation.** A reply suggests Hyperframes. Another links a repository that generates a timeline file for import into Resolve, an alternative to controlling the editor interactively. A cautionary reply raises accidental file operations but does not document an incident.

### The science behind ordinary products

[Original source: @YouTubeAut3538](https://x.com/YouTubeAut3538/status/2098779054736396619)

A repeatable editorial lens connects familiar products to design and business decisions.

The screenshot shows The Science of Products. Examples connect Uniqlo to deliberately plain clothes, Casio to durability and IKEA to low-cost design. The format begins with something recognizable, then explains the mechanism that made it successful.

**Replies and continuation.** No substantive reply was exposed in the public sample.

**Assessment.** One of the strongest fits for your interests. GPUs, liquidation lots, mechanical keyboards and local AI all offer concrete trade-offs to explain. The repeatable element should be the question, while each story supplies different evidence.


### Does sharing an IP reduce impressions?

[Original source: @egoo_58](https://x.com/egoo_58/status/2098874248559300921)

The author asserts a rule that the replies immediately dispute.

The post claims that too many channels on one IP receive low impressions and recommends proxies and an antidetect browser, naming AdsPower. It also refers to association between channels during demonetization.

**Replies and continuation.** One reader reports a proxy channel failing to load. Others reject the explanation; one offers a competing trust-score theory and examples of creators with many channels. Neither side supplies a controlled test.

**Assessment.** Unsubstantiated causal advice. The conversation does not demonstrate that IP separation fixes impressions. Keep it out of a content strategy until credible platform evidence or a properly controlled investigation supports it.


Related evidence: [Reply / quoted source: @Champion_manny](https://x.com/Champion_manny/status/2098887290542235834); [Reply / quoted source: @altwhis](https://x.com/altwhis/status/2098888552398639171); [Reply / quoted source: @SethfowIermad](https://x.com/SethfowIermad/status/2098892933156254040).


### Fifteen channels, one monetization failure

[Original source: @thegoldeenhand](https://x.com/thegoldeenhand/status/2099202146361352665)

An anecdote about connected channels leads into a multiple-account sales pitch.

The author describes a member losing monetization across 15 channels after an inauthentic-content action associated with one AdSense account. The story is used to promote an account-structure offer. No case documents or appeal outcome are provided.

**Replies and continuation.** The accessible discussion does not independently establish the cause of the reported enforcement.

**Assessment.** Do not turn the proposed account workaround into operating advice. Google states that publishers may maintain only one AdSense account. YouTube’s monetization policy addresses repetitive or mass-produced content and warns against circumventing restrictions through related channels. Editorial originality matters more than an account diagram.


Related evidence: [Google: one AdSense account](https://support.google.com/adsense/answer/9729); [YouTube monetization policies](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1311392).


### AI ASMR: image to shot specification

[Original source: @0xForce_](https://x.com/0xForce_/status/2099665370697068573)

The workflow converts a reference image into a detailed video prompt.

The spoken tutorial starts with a Pinterest reference image, asks Claude for an ASMR video prompt, then uses Picsart’s AI Playground with the reference and prompt. It names Veo 3.1 and shows a portrait, eight-second, audio-enabled generation setup. Picsart was confirmed visually after speech recognition misheard the name. The post emphasizes material texture, motion and sound.

**Replies and continuation.** No substantive visible reply established attributable channel earnings.

**Assessment.** The reported $10K–$30K/month is hearsay here. The useful production idea is to specify what moves, what the material looks like and what sound should follow. Test whether the generator actually synchronizes sound with the action.


### Puffi: tiny creature, oversized ASMR obstacles

[Original source: @hipuffi](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdEGrXXCGKu/)

A 13-second Roblox-style parkour clip through a pastel food world.

The caption describes purple dumplings and rainbow-cake ASMR parkour. The footage puts a tiny avatar among giant smiling purple shapes and pale rounded stepping surfaces, in a lavender checkerboard environment. Its appeal comes from the scale mismatch, tactile materials, a clear route and repeated landings. The downloaded audio produced no intelligible speech in the local transcription pass.

**Replies and continuation.** Visible comments mostly express affection or imitate the creature; one asks whether it is a game. The sample did not expose a substantive creator reply or production method.

**Assessment.** A useful sensory reference for the meowl keyboard garden and this website. Borrow the relationship between creature, surface and reaction, while creating your own objects and interactions. This is a short-form format reference, not evidence of a YouTube business.

## Design


### Polish the working build

[Original source: @noclipepe](https://x.com/noclipepe/status/2099937335437602996)

Compare the existing result to a reference and repair the largest visible differences.

The prompt preserves the working game and focuses the next pass on character fidelity, proportions, lighting, camera behavior, transitions, physics and the elements that still look generic. Its quoted demo compares a recreated fishing game to a reference.

**Replies and continuation.** The adjacent comparison clips are demonstrations, not a reproducible benchmark of general game-building ability.

**Assessment.** Directly useful here: keep interactions that work, identify specific visual gaps, then check the result again. We used this approach for the habitat’s scale, mobile framing and label placement.


Related evidence: [Author continuation: @noclipepe](https://x.com/noclipepe/status/2099278496509952485); [Author continuation: @noclipepe](https://x.com/noclipepe/status/2099937284241891720).


### Write the message before choosing the decoration

[Original source: @dickiebush](https://x.com/dickiebush/status/2100653530176430270)

Dickie Bush’s linked guide separates personal evidence, copy review and visual direction.

The full article starts with a plain-language offer worksheet, then checks vague claims, repetitive phrasing and generic AI language. Its design exercise collects reference screenshots, names preferences for type, color, surfaces and layout, compares three directions using the same copy, and refines the strongest. Later sections cover implementation, explanatory visuals, mobile review and deployment.

**Replies and continuation.** Replies reinforce using customer language and checking whether the reader can understand the offer. The article links its worksheets and examples and promotes a writing product.

**Assessment.** Strong process reference. For your personal site, we used actual projects and your meowl direction as the raw material. No testimonials, income figures or conversion claims were invented. The article’s deployment instructions were not treated as instructions to alter your accounts.

## Other


### A second brain that maintains its own notes

[Original source: @rvaniaaaa](https://x.com/rvaniaaaa/status/2099065255259156843)

Keep original sources, then build a linked wiki that can be corrected and queried.

The root post describes an initially unrewarding setup period. Its quoted article proposes raw inputs, a maintained wiki, outputs and a governing instruction file. New material updates existing concepts, links related pages and flags contradictions. The author also proposes a personal-profile interview, project folders and a recurring maintenance brief.

**Replies and continuation.** Public replies describe the same slow start and raise operational accountability. They do not establish a source-count threshold.

**Assessment.** Useful architecture; overstated certainty. The article’s 50–100-source threshold is anecdotal, and its paid-Claude-only framing is narrower than Karpathy’s tool-agnostic original. Karpathy’s April gist explicitly leaves implementation choices open. Preserve provenance so an incorrect summary does not become its own evidence.

### Seven business prompts, translated into decisions

[Original source: @jorgerebollo_ia](https://x.com/jorgerebollo_ia/status/2099599077910438297)

Audit what you can already do, find a paid problem and test an offer.

The seven Spanish continuations cover: inventorying skills and resources; spotting overlooked assets; finding problems customers already pay to solve; attacking a business idea skeptically; defining offers at different service levels; planning a low-resource first 30 days; and forming a 90-day strategy with distractions to stop. These are English reading notes rather than verbatim translations.

**Replies and continuation.** The author’s complete seven-part prompt sequence was recovered. The useful progression moves from personal evidence to customer demand and an executable offer.

**Assessment.** Useful questions, not market validation. For your hardware pipeline, the missing evidence would be an actual buyer, an available lot, testable condition and a resale comparison after fees. Prompt quality cannot supply those facts.

### Fourteen agents and a long-running experiment

[Original source: @SPAC89](https://x.com/SPAC89/status/2100126725988360661)

An author reports a 165-minute multi-agent run with repeated scoring rounds.

The post describes independent judges and a self-imposed quality threshold of 9.5 before completion. A screenshot and quoted earlier test accompany the claim. A later author reply reports another run lasting more than 90 minutes and says its limits are separate from Codex.

**Replies and continuation.** A reader reports that their account exposes no subagent tools. That is a material counterexample to treating the reported setup as universally available.

**Assessment.** A workflow anecdote. A model-generated score is not external validation, and more agents or elapsed time do not prove quality. The claims about access and unlimited usage were not verified as account-independent product rules.

### Remote-work links behind a broad headline

[Original source: @sadhna6389](https://x.com/sadhna6389/status/2100056808207581444)

Seven job boards, a resume tool and a newsletter offer are presented as nine job sites.

The recovered sequence names Kickresume; a virtual-assistant newsletter offer; Working Nomads; Remote OK; Remote.co; AngelList; Remotive; Himalayas; and We Work Remotely. The first two are not equivalent to browsing an employer’s open roles. The thread repeatedly attaches high hourly-pay claims without linking specific qualifying vacancies.

**Replies and continuation.** A reader objects to pay-to-play services and suggests another job-search product. That alternative was not independently evaluated.

**Assessment.** Use the list as discovery leads only. The post does not establish that every role is worldwide, open to everyone or paid at the advertised rate. Verify location, employment terms and eligibility on each employer’s own posting.

### AI employees: the complete four-stage structure

[Original source: @hooeem](https://x.com/hooeem/status/2100599265944867326)

The sixteen prompt images describe discovery, responsibility design, implementation and testing.

Stage one maps objectives, workflows, missing work and constraints. Stage two allocates work to automation, reusable skills, ongoing agents or people, and challenges unnecessary roles. Stage three defines each selected role’s triggers, authoritative inputs, decisions, tools, memory, outputs and action permissions before picking a runtime. Stage four tests failures, monitors real work, controls rollout and sends new evidence back into the role design.

**Replies and continuation.** All four image sets were recovered and OCR-read, including the three author continuations. Each phase passes a written handoff and structured state packet into the next. A commenter asks whether managing the prompts becomes a job itself.

**Assessment.** The durable idea is explicit responsibility plus measurable performance. A prompt package alone does not create working integrations or prove useful autonomy. Use the smallest workable setup and measure the review burden.

### Ask for a better brief first

[Original source: @eng_khairallah1](https://x.com/eng_khairallah1/status/2101631838888374440)

The image prompt separates literal wording from the problem the user is trying to solve.

The prompt asks the model to identify the underlying objective, inspect ambiguities, distinguish stated facts from assumptions, expose constraints and produce a clearer task with acceptance criteria. The quoted article expands into a broader prompting guide. The longer guide advocates explicit deliverables, labelled reference materials, task boundaries, effort matched to consequence, mid-task steering and observable verification. Its model-performance assertions were not independently verified.

**Replies and continuation.** The visible replies are positive reactions rather than comparisons against a baseline.

**Assessment.** Useful when a request is genuinely underspecified. It should not become a mandatory interrogation before every small action. A better brief can reduce ambiguity; it cannot guarantee a better answer or recover missing evidence.

## Where to find excellent personal websites


- [Godly](https://godly.design/): Expressive layouts, unusual portfolios and sites with a strong visual premise.


- [One Page Love: personal](https://onepagelove.com/genre/personal): Compact personal websites. Study how much identity fits into one page.


- [Curated Design](https://www.curated.design/): A broad visual reference library. Use its portfolio category to narrow the search.


- [SiteInspire](https://www.siteinspire.com/): Useful for type, layout, spacing and restrained editorial choices.


- [Awwwards: portfolios](https://www.awwwards.com/websites/portfolio/): A discovery lead for experimental portfolios; the category page timed out in this session.


- [Lapa Ninja](https://www.lapa.ninja/): Landing-page references named in the linked Dickie Bush guide.


- [Rauno](https://rauno.me/): Confidence in scale, intentional empty space and small interaction details. The rendered page was inspected.


- [Dennis Snellenberg](https://dennissnellenberg.com/): Strong visual presence and large typographic movement. The rendered page was inspected.


- [Bruno Simon](https://bruno-simon.com/): A navigable personal world. The principle is to make exploration itself express the creator.


## Turn browsing into design skill

Choose three references with different strengths: one for typography, one for layout and one for interaction. Write down the actual decision you admire, such as the ratio between headline and body type, the alignment of a hero, or how a control settles after release. Save that observation with the reference.

Rebuild one section privately to understand its geometry, then create a different section using the same principle and your own content. Compare the rendered result at a wide and a narrow viewport. Fix the largest discrepancy first. Repeat on a bounded section instead of collecting another hundred screenshots.

Use motion to show cause and effect. A selected object can lean toward you; a released drag can settle; a key can compress. Keep the reading position stable. Make the same action work with a keyboard and respect reduced-motion preferences. A memorable interaction should still leave the visitor able to find the work.

The redesigned site uses DM Serif Display and IBM Plex Sans, mineral grey surfaces and original code-drawn meowls. Its main sequence follows a fictional interview through a HALO prompt to an answer. The galleries are inspiration sources; their layouts and artwork were not copied.
